headline: RBA holds rates at 4.35% with a hawkish warning, PLS.AX gets smacked 4.5%, and GOOG surges 2.5% in a strong session for US tech.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a rough session today, dropping 4.5% to $6.19. Despite recent positive commentary around a lithium sector rebound and Pilbara commissioning a new lithium facility, the market sold off today — likely spooked by the RBA's hawkish tone (keeping rates high dampens economic sentiment) and oil's sharp fall weighing on commodities broadly. The stock is still well below its all-time highs, and the lithium recovery story is far from guaranteed.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL fell 2.1% today to $8.29, dragged down by a sharp drop in crude oil prices — WTI oil fell over 3% to $78.20/barrel. Goldman Sachs has reportedly cut its oil price forecast, and a potential US-Iran peace deal is adding supply expectations to the market. Less demand for oil = lower oil company profits = lower FUEL price.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG had a solid session last night, jumping 2.5% to $367.11. No single major catalyst was reported — it appears to be broad tech sector strength lifting Alphabet along with it. Your GOOG position is now up 27% overall, a strong result.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI gained 1.2% today to $18.07, riding the AI sentiment wave. News around AI regulation and new model launches (including China's Zhipu AI releasing its GLM-5.2 model) kept the sector in the spotlight. Still sitting about 5% below your cost base overall, but momentum is improving.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 0.5% today to $528.17, reflecting last night's positive US market session. The ASX-listed version tracks the full US sharemarket, so it benefits when US equities are broadly up. Now sitting slightly in the green overall.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE nudged up 0.4% to $94.74 — a quiet but positive session. Emerging markets got a small lift, possibly helped by China AI news and a slightly weaker US dollar. Just barely in the green overall at +0.94% total return.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was essentially flat today, ticking up just 3 cents to $77.25. As a diversified fund spread across global shares, bonds, and property, it doesn't move dramatically on any single day — which is the whole point. Up 2.5% overall from your cost base.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: No updated price data available for MSFT today — last close was $390.74 USD. Nothing major in the news to flag. US markets open tonight around 11:30 PM AEST, so watch for any movement then.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: No updated price data for TTWO today — last close was $211.75 USD. The good news: an insider has pushed back on rumours that Rockstar is delaying GTA 6 into 2027, which should be a mild positive for sentiment when US markets open tonight.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Hold through the pain
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped 4.5% today to $6.19, and you're now 8.2% underwater on this position. The lithium rebound story is still being talked up (new facility commissioned, sector sentiment improving), but today's sell-off shows how volatile this one is. No new fundamental reason to sell — hold and watch for any lithium price data this week.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Oil is sliding, stay cautious
watch_today.detail: Crude oil dropped over 3% last night to $78.20/barrel, and Goldman Sachs has cut its oil price forecast. A potential US-Iran peace deal is also being discussed, which would add more oil supply to the market. FUEL fell 2.1% today and is marginally in the red overall. If oil keeps sliding, expect more pressure here.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Riding high, hold comfortably
watch_today.detail: GOOG jumped 2.5% last night to $367.11, and your position is now up 27% overall. No specific catalyst — just broad tech strength. Nothing to do here except enjoy it. US markets open tonight, watch for any follow-through.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 delay rumour shot down
watch_today.detail: An insider has reportedly dismissed rumours that Rockstar is pushing GTA 6 into 2027. If true, this removes one of the key bearish risks for Take-Two. No updated price yet (US markets open tonight ~11:30 PM AEST), but this is a mild positive going into the session.

watch_today.title: RBA held rates — but warned they could hike again
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank kept the cash rate at 4.35% today, as widely expected. However, Governor Michele Bullock explicitly said 'if we need to increase again, we will.' That's a hawkish (rate-hike-leaning) signal that could weigh on growth stocks and property. Keep this in mind — it's not a 'rates are coming down soon' situation.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI momentum building, but still underwater
watch_today.detail: GXAI gained 1.2% today and AI news flow remains strong (US regulation concerns, new Chinese models, broad sector interest). You're still 5% below your cost base, but the trend is improving. Hold and let the thesis play out.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a cracking day, jumping 1.3% to close at 8,917 — a solid broad-market rally. The RBA's rate hold was well telegraphed, so markets largely shrugged off the hawkish tone. Crude oil was the big mover overnight, tumbling 3.2% to $78.20/barrel on Goldman Sachs cutting forecasts and US-Iran peace deal speculation. Gold ticked up 0.65% to $4,356/oz, holding near record levels. The Aussie dollar was largely flat at 70.6 US cents. US indices (S&P 500 and NASDAQ) don't have updated prices yet — those sessions run tonight.

politics.summary: The RBA dominated the news today, holding rates steady but making clear it's not done hiking if needed. There's also movement on a potential CGT (capital gains tax) carve-out that could affect property and investment decisions.

stories.title: RBA holds cash rate at 4.35% — but Bullock warns hikes aren't off the table
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank kept Australia's official interest rate on hold at 4.35% today, as most economists expected. But Governor Michele Bullock didn't soften her tone — she explicitly warned that 'if we need to increase again, we will.' That's a signal that rate cuts aren't coming any time soon, and anyone with a variable mortgage or investment loan shouldn't bank on relief just yet. Analysts are calling this a 'hawkish pause' — meaning the RBA is holding its fire but keeping its options open to strike again.

stories.title: Government may fast-track CGT carve-outs amid growing criticism
stories.why_it_matters: The Federal Government is reportedly considering fast-tracking exemptions to its proposed capital gains tax (CGT) reforms — a tax on investment profits — after significant pushback. The original proposal would increase the effective tax on investment gains, hitting property investors and share traders hardest. By carving out certain assets or situations, the Government is trying to soften the blow. If you hold investment properties or have large unrealised gains in your portfolio, this is worth watching closely as the detail emerges.

stories.title: Aussies warned rate relief may be short-lived after RBA decision
stories.why_it_matters: Analysts quoted by Nine are warning that even if the RBA eventually cuts rates, any reprieve for borrowers could be short-lived if inflation proves sticky. With Bullock flagging another potential hike, economists are split on whether we see a cut before year-end. The practical upshot: don't lock in fixed rates expecting a big drop — the path is genuinely uncertain right now.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is the US government moving to restrict Anthropic's AI — a sign that AI regulation is getting very real, very fast. Meanwhile, China's Zhipu AI launched a new model that sent its stock rocketing, and the debate around AI regulation in financial services is heating up globally.

stories.title: US curbs Anthropic AI, rattling the broader sector
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has moved to restrict or take down one of Anthropic's AI models, sending a shockwave through the AI industry. Critics are warning this represents 'ad hoc' regulation — meaning decisions made on the fly without a clear legal framework, which creates uncertainty for companies building on these tools. For your AI-exposed holdings like GXAI.AX and GOOG (which competes with Anthropic via Gemini), unpredictable regulatory moves in the US are a risk worth watching. The Hill reports that industry voices are pushing for a more structured regulatory approach rather than case-by-case government interventions.

stories.title: China's Zhipu AI stock rockets after launching GLM-5.2 model
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese AI firm Zhipu AI saw its stock surge after launching its new GLM-5.2 model, adding to the evidence that China is mounting a serious challenge to US AI dominance. This is relevant to your VGE.AX (emerging markets ETF, which has China exposure) and to the broader competitive landscape for GOOG and MSFT. A strong Chinese AI ecosystem means Google and Microsoft face real global competition, not just from each other.

stories.title: AI regulation in financial services heating up globally
stories.why_it_matters: Both KPMG and BBVA published major pieces today on how to regulate AI in banking and finance. The key tension: AI is moving faster than governments can write rules for it, and financial regulators globally are trying to catch up. For investors in AI-exposed stocks and ETFs, more regulation generally means higher compliance costs but also more certainty long-term. Isaac Asimov's fictional 'three laws of robotics' are even being cited as a framework — which tells you how early-stage this regulatory thinking still is.

stories.title: Americans strongly back AI regulation, new survey finds
stories.why_it_matters: A new survey shows strong majority support among Americans for government regulation of AI. This matters because it gives US politicians the public mandate to act — meaning tighter AI rules are likely coming regardless of which party is in power. Companies like Google and Microsoft that are deepest into AI will face the most scrutiny, but they're also best placed to shape the rules given their lobbying resources.

sport.summary: Round 16 NRL teams are dropping and there's injury and selection news to digest before the weekend. On the AFL front, South Australia has locked in Gather Round until 2029, and the Socceroos are caught up in a controversy over scheduling.

stories.title: Round 16 team lists out — flag favourites face 'scary new reality'
stories.why_it_matters: Round 16 team lists are out ahead of the weekend. Fox Sports is flagging a 'scary new reality' for flag favourites — suggesting some of the competition heavyweights have selection or form issues heading in. The Bulldogs get a boost with a concussed star reportedly returning. Broncos, Eels, and Rabbitohs are all on the bye this week. Your local Gold Coast Titans host the Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium on Saturday at 5:30 PM — a massive game given Penrith's form.

stories.title: 'Devastating' Luai truth after Tigers admission; Eels face halves dilemma
stories.why_it_matters: There's drama at Wests Tigers, with a 'devastating' admission around Jarome Luai's situation at the club — Fox Sports is suggesting the Tigers have admitted something significant about his future or form that's a blow to their season. Meanwhile, a shock rise from a player at the Eels has created a genuine selection headache at halfback or five-eighth, with Parramatta reportedly unsure who to pair in their halves going forward.

stories.title: South Australia locks in AFL Gather Round until 2029
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia has secured a deal to host the AFL's Gather Round — where all teams play in Adelaide over one weekend — through to 2029. It's been a massive economic win for SA, bringing thousands of interstate visitors and tens of millions in tourism spend each year. The extension to 2029 cements Gather Round as a permanent fixture on the AFL calendar, giving clubs, fans, and sponsors certainty to plan ahead.

stories.title: 'It's a disgrace': Anger over 'deliberate' move around the Socceroos
stories.why_it_matters: There's fury in Australian football circles over what's being described as a 'deliberate' move to disadvantage the Socceroos — though the article text isn't available to confirm exact details. The language used ('it's a disgrace') suggests a scheduling, broadcasting, or administrative decision that's perceived as working against Australia's national men's football team. Worth keeping an eye on as more details emerge.
